decisions.mechanismComparison: Chorus already owns claim-provenance editorial briefs, channel-native drafts, derivatives, and accessible media briefs, while Muse owns the companion visual system and acceptance boundaries.
decisions.rationale: Keep the Wave 2 pair as additional evaluated evidence for the existing Chorus and Muse composition instead of creating duplicate editorial or visual ownership.

decisions.mechanismComparison: Chorus verifies claims, accessibility, and local editorial artifacts but does not currently own Open Graph or platform-card field mapping, absolute image reachability, dimension checks, or cache-oriented preview diagnostics.
decisions.rationale: Add one read-first preview-verification specialization under Chorus without granting publication, account access, or platform mutation authority.

decisions.mechanismComparison: Chorus already separates source-labeled listening, response triage, current-signal research, validated analysis, community policy, and human escalation from all live account action.
decisions.rationale: The Wave 2 review reinforces an existing stronger stewardship route and does not justify a second monitoring owner.

decisions.mechanismComparison: Beacon already owns evidence-bounded market, competitor, audience, message, experiment, and growth analysis while preserving paid-account, budget, attribution, privacy, and external-effect boundaries.
decisions.rationale: Route this public-ad research evidence to Beacon rather than widening Chorus or creating another competitive-intelligence capability.
